# SCI-FRUIT v0.1 — EL-G0 Candidate-Family And Resource Frame r0.1

Status: **bounded family proposal; no recurrence, prototype, run, or resource
allocation is approved**

## Mandatory Control

Every development unit runs the exact approved `historical_scientific_control`
on the paired input. The control is not one of the candidate methods and is not
truth. No candidate ranking occurs if control identity or output validity
fails.

## Proposed Candidate-Family Bound

Gate D should admit no more than three recurrence families in its first
generation:

1. **Complete-product replacement family.** Preserve the historical state
   replacement form while varying only prospectively listed model-selection,
   causal adaptation, or stopping policies. This tests whether much of the
   gain comes from policy rather than a new numerical recurrence.
2. **Relaxed complete-product transition family.** Given a complete proposed
   next state `F_tilde`, study a bounded relaxation such as
   `F_{k+1}=F_k+alpha_k(F_tilde-F_k)` only after common representation,
   response, support, grid/WCS, and causal semantics are defined. This is an
   intentional new law unless equivalence is proved.
3. **Response-aware residual-correction family.** Apply a bounded, explicitly
   response/support-aware correction derived from the new residual record to
   the accepted state. Ordinary unqualified increment accumulation is not an
   admissible member.

The family names define research questions, not algorithms. Gate D must supply
each exact recurrence, state schema, finite parameter grid, causal adaptation
inputs, bounds, terminal policy, checkpoint state, and expected difference
from history before any prototype is run.

## Search And Submission Caps

The proposed first generation permits:

- at most three recurrence families;
- at most two exact policy/parameter variants per family and profile in the
  initial development tranche;
- no unrecorded manual variants;
- one immutable development ledger including failed and abandoned candidates;
- no more than three exact method/claim submissions total to Gate F, including
  any broad method and profile specializations; and
- a new generation for every post-freeze method or protocol change.

These caps are candidates for owner review. Exact finite parameter values are
still unavailable.

## Resource Evidence And Boundary

Historical repository tooling proposed per-job limits of 24 wall-clock hours,
64 GiB memory, six CPUs, and array concurrency four while snapshotting the
binary and hashing configs. Those values are historical operational evidence,
not approved Gate-D limits and not performance measurements.

Before Gate D, the execution plan must bind:

```text
maximum independent development units
maximum control and candidate jobs
maximum iterations and terminal caps per METHOD_ID
CPU/GPU type and concurrency
per-job wall time and memory
aggregate CPU/GPU-hour ceiling
input/output/read/write and retained-storage ceilings
checkpoint and failure-retry policy
human Unity operator and review cadence
automatic stop on budget, validity, or contamination breach
```

No performance-derived budget can be inferred without opening historical
outcomes. The owner may authorize a small feasibility tranche later, or may
require a human-supplied outcome-free resource inventory before setting the
Gate-D envelope.

## Retention

Permanent retention is required for exact configs/manifests, method and claim
identities, source/environment records, terminal products, required metric
sufficient statistics, failures/incidents, and causal checkpoint state.
Per-iteration maps and update contributions may use a bounded diagnostic
horizon or reconstructible tier unless a metric or exact restart requires
them. Stable identity does not imply unbounded retention.
